articles.title: "He would stare at dudes' meat" – Paul George exposes disturbing behavior by reporter in NBA locker room
articles.summary: “PG-13” confirmed there are male reporters strangely staring at players' meat in locker rooms
articles.body:
The NBA locker room has traditionally been one of basketball's most important spaces as it offers players a place to prepare, recover and decompress. However, the league's longstanding policy of allowing reporters inside has raised questions about how much privacy players should surrender in exchange for media access.

All-Star guard Paul George brought the debate back into focus when he described how uncomfortable the experience was involving reporters, specifically males, entering the locker room while they were still undressed.

For George and his fellow NBA players, the final buzzer does not necessarily mean the working day is over. After competing for 48 minutes, they still have to shower, refresh and mentally process what happened before facing questions from journalists.

PG believes the media's presence during that vulnerable period creates an unnecessary invasion of privacy.

"You got to understand, bro, like, the game might be over and 10 minutes after that, all the reporters are coming in, I would say majority of the locker room, bro, they're naked, like, we're in towels, we're naked, we just got out the shower and then you have these reporters in there," George said on "Podcast P."

George recalled an NBA reporter's strange behavior

Paul's concern was not limited to being interviewed immediately after a game. He also questioned whether these journalists could maintain appropriate boundaries or even understand that they exist.

As he tackled the issue, George was reminded of an incident in which male NBA reporters crossed the players' boundaries by deciding to discuss what they had seen inside the locker room.

George also recalled a very uncomfortable moment in which another male reporter was unapologetically checking them out.

"There was an incident where guys would talk about this situation," George said. "There was a reporter in Washington that would stare at dudes' meat while they're, like, you know, changing."

George did not publicly identify the journalist mentioned above. Moreover, his allegation should be understood as his personal account.

Another NBA star also had a locker room issue

George wasn't the only NBA personality who has shared his locker room experiences in public. In October 2021, former New Jersey Nets forward Richard Jefferson publicly confronted an NBA ballboy over an identical issue.

RJ was upset after the ballboy accused him of being rude on TikTok. In a fiery response, Jefferson blasted the ballboy and relentlessly called him out for not only staring at his penis while inside the locker room but also comparing it with other NBA players.

"You literally admit to looking at our junks when we were in the locker room…And this is another thing that I want people to really observe here. You're not just saying, 'Ooh I saw Richard's junk.' No. You're talking about in comparison to other men in the locker room," Jefferson exclaimed.

"The biggest you saw. Well, it might be true," he continued. "The point is, that is why I did not interact with you… That's why I didn't talk to you, because you were looking at our junks the whole time. And you felt so comfortable, you decided, 'I don't mind. I'll do TikToks and talk about comparing grown men's junks in the locker room."

NBA locker room policies and the ongoing privacy debate

The NBA allows locker room access to give reporters opportunities to interview players after games. However, when access resumed for the 2022-23 season, the league introduced stricter rules, allowing Tier 1 media members inside the arena 30 minutes before games, after a 20-minute cooling-off period. Other journalists must use designated media areas.

While the NBA has already addressed the issue with its reasonable policies, former NBPA executive Michele Roberts criticized the practice as an invasion of privacy back in 2015. She questioned the need for reporters to remain when they had no questions after regularly seeing them "just staring" at the players.

As it stands, the NBA seems to have found a balance between media access and players' privacy. However, that doesn't guarantee that what George and Jefferson experienced wouldn't happen again.

This story was originally published by Basketball Network on Nov 15, 2026, where it first appeared in the Off The Court section. Add Basketball Network as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

articles.title: Kate Van Appledorn powers Calvin to five-set comeback thriller over Hope for MIAA title
articles.summary: Another five-set thriller in the Hope-Calvin volleyball rivalry as the Knights come back to win in 5 to reach NCAA tournament.
articles.body:
Hope College vs. Calvin women's volleyball photo gallery

GRAND RAPIDS - Tied 10-10 in the fifth set, Hope's top hitter looked ready to slam a kill and seize the momentum.

Calvin's Kate Van Appledorn had other ideas.

The Holland Christian graduate blocked the spike, then tipped a kill on the next play to lead the Knights to a comeback win in five sets to claim the MIAA Tournament title and earn the automatic bid to the NCAA Division III Tournament on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Van Noord Arena.

"It was so exciting. I just try to be available in pressure situations and show confidence because I trust my team and they trust me," Van Appledorn said. "I was more ready as a blocker. We are so excited to have this confidence going into the NCAA tournament."

The Knights won 21-25, 25-20, 20-25, 25-21, 15-12 to head to the NCAA tournament at 25-3.

The fifth set was tied at 3-5-6-7-9-9-10-12 before MIAA MVP Sarah Bradley put a kill down and the Knights hung on.

"Hope played good defense and did well with their serving. They are much improved from the last time we saw them. Halfway through the fourth set, we talked about playing to win instead of not playing to lose. That really flipped us," Calvin coach Amber Warners said. "Kate is getting more confidence and we are working on getting her a more efficient arm swing. I think she played with a little chip on her shoulder tonight, wanting to show what she can do. Nothing shakes her, and we needed her tonight."

Van Appledorn finished with 11 kills and four blocks.

Hope finished the season 19-9. A season that saw the Flying Dutch knock off the No. 1 team in the country, and finish a couple of points from the automatic bid to the NCAA tournament.

"It was a hard-fought match for sure. It was a battle of first contact. We served tough, but we had a hard time timing our block against their outsides," Hope coach Becky Schmidt said. "We really wanted it for our seniors to be able to have a shot at continuing this ride a little bit longer."

It is the first time Hope will not be in the NCAA tournament since 2017 and just the second time since 2005.

Hope senior Kamryn Burbridge passed 1,000 career kills in the match.

It came in the third set, putting the Flying Dutch up 17-15 in set they would win.

Burbridge and libero Kathryn Oates are the seniors in the regular rotation that will graduate.

Burbridge was All-MIAA all four seasons as a middle hitter. She was all-region the past two.

She had nine kills and four blocks in the match.

"Kam has been our rock all season," Schmidt said. "She is one of the most dynamic, if not the most dynamic middle we have ever had in our program. Her blocking, attacking, she is playing on another level."

"Kate Oates is just a champ." Schmidt said.

The first set was tied at 13-14-15-16-17. A Hope ace made it 18-17 and forced a Calvin timeout. Another ace by Brooke Hehl pushed the lead to 20-17 and the Knights took their second timeout.

Angie Butler slammed a kill before Hope put down a huge block to lead 22-17, a 5-0 run. Butler put another one down and Kiera Morrison slammed two to win it 25-21. Butler put down seven kills in the opening set.

The second set saw Calvin out to a 10-5 lead. Hope pulled within 16-15 after a couple of kills from Maddie Ostrander. But the Knights didn't give up the lead and hung on for a 25-21 win on an ace from Lina Kasuboski to tie the match 1-1.

Hope built a 5-1 lead to start the third. Burbridge made it 8-3 with a crosscourt kill. Ostrander kept going with a kill then an ace to push it to 14-10. Morrison put down two big kills to make it 22-19. Burbridge added another and Amelia Gagnon aced a serve on set point for a 25-20 win and a 2-1 lead in the set.

In the fourth, Tryna VanderZwaag served up an ace to put the Knights up 8-6. An ace from Kasuboski and block by Sarah Bradley pushed the lead to 14-10. A kill from Kate Van Appledorn made it 17-13, a tip as the Knights found success with tipping. She then slammed one in the middle for a 20-16 lead and the Knights won 25-21 to send it to a fifth set.

Butler finished with 18 kills to lead Hope, Morrison had 17 and Ostrander had eight to go along with six blocks.

Hehl dished out 45 assists and added nine digs. Oates finished with 21 digs and Gagnon had 14.

The Knights were led by Bradley with 21 kills and 20 digs. VanderZwaag had 22 digs and eight assists. Olivia Peterson posted 47 assists.

articles.title: Heat’s Bam Adebayo starts Most Improved Player campaign for Davion Mitchell
articles.summary: MIAMI – With the Miami Heat looking to reach their ceiling led by Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, other pieces on the team will be vital if the franc...
articles.body:
MIAMI – With the Miami Heat looking to reach their ceiling led by Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, other pieces on the team will be vital if the franchise wants to reach new heights this season. One example of the Heat being a dangerous force in the NBA came in Friday night's 133-121 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers , as aside from the two star big men, point guard Davion Mitchell played a pivotal role.

Sure, Antetokounmpo and Adebayo each recorded 37 points and collected 23 rebounds between the two of them, but Mitchell was a key engine in the offense. The 28-year-old scored 22 points on seven of 14 shooting from the field and three of seven from deep, but it was the whopping 17 assists that stood out in the stat sheet, as it tied his career-high from his rookie year with the Sacramento Kings.

Heat's Bam Adebayo believes Davion Mitchell deserves NBA award

The 17 assists are tied for second-most in a game by a Miami player with Goran Dragic in 2016 and Sherman Douglas in 1990, with the No. spot belonging to Tim Hardaway Sr. with 18 in 1996. While the 17 assists were impressive, Mitchell has been effective all season as the team's primary point guard and a defensive force.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Averaging the most minutes on the team with 36 per game, he's also recorded 16.9 points and 9.2 assists per contest while shooting 49.7 percent from the field and 40.6 percent from three-point range. Through 10 games, Mitchell has figured it out, leading to Adebayo saying after Friday's win that Mitchell should get the award for the NBA's Most Improved Player (MIP).

"Davion [Mitchell], I want him to get the Most Improved [Player award] for sure," Adebayo said. "Davion is making great reads. He's done a great job of making the game easier for all of us…. This is showing all the work he put in all summer. It's good to see him be in shape and really be himself."

If there was another aspect of Mitchell's performance that was impressive aside from the 17 assists, it was that the guard had just one turnover. Last season, Mitchell's assist-to-turnover ratio ranked among the best in the NBA, so it's no doubt encouraging to see the outing, with Antetokounmpo applauding his teammate.

"Incredible, 17 assists," Antetokounmpo said. "The most impressive thing is one turnover. That's insane. He keeps making the right play, setting the tone, knocking down shots. He's pretty much doing everything for us. He stepped his game up this year big time."

Heat's Erik Spoelstra on the "progression" of Davion Mitchell

There's no denying that Mitchell came into this season with a purpose, working diligently in the summer to improve and gain chemistry with Antetokounmpo and Adebayo. Subsequently, head coach Erik Spoelstra noticed the change in his shape heading into the year.

"Well, he's in fantastic shape," Mitchell said to ClutchPoints before Saturday night's game against the Pistons. "Really, by early summer, he had really started working on it. And in the year and a half before that, with us, he had shown the flashes that he could do a lot of these types of things; it was just about having more endurance, more stamina, to be able to make more plays and impose his speed and quickness and physicality on the game."

"And I just think you're seeing a progression," Spoelstra continued. "Those at the end of the first year, we had those two playing games where he was fantastic for us, and then the next year, last year, you know, he had moments where he was really good, and now he's just able to sustain that. And we want to have guys run with him. He's fast with the ball, and he's unselfish. He wants to set guys up."

Right now, Mitchell is third with +1000 odds at FanDuel Sportsbook to win the NBA MIP for the 2026-27 season. Mitchell emphasized that his job is to feed his teammates the ball and get them into rhythm, and he's doing that thus far, as it remains to be seen if Adebayo's request for the guard to be MIP will come to fruition.

articles.title: Cavaliers backups beat Mavericks as all 5 Cleveland starters sit out Saturday night's win
articles.summary: Tyrese Proctor capitalized on the opportunity and finished with a triple-double.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Dallas Mavericks 127-117 on Saturday night.

While the win itself is notable — Cleveland entered the game at 6-7 and Dallas at 7-5 — the story was the players the Cavaliers won with.

Saturday night was Cleveland's second game in a back-to-back. The Cavs were in Miami on Friday night and lost 133-121. With the nationwide domestic flight ground stop lasting four hours on Friday, travel plans across sports leagues were impacted.

Cleveland's game finished after the ground stop ended, but the decision had already been made for the Cavaliers to fly back home Saturday morning. The team landed in Cleveland around noon local time, and then had a quick turnaround for Saturday night's game.

The Cavaliers ruled out all five of their usual starters. James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen were inactive ahead of the game.

This led Cleveland to start Mario Hezonja, Thomas Bryant, Jaylon Tyson, Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas against a full-strength Mavericks squad.

Proctor led the way with a triple-double. He finished with 24 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Hezonja added 22 points, while Bryant had 19 points and 11 boards.

Cleveland's bench was shallow with only three players used, but they had an impact. Not only did the three eat up necessary minutes, but Norchad Omier had 13 points and eight rebounds, while Craig Porter Jr. added 9 points, 9 rebounds and 6 assists.

Dallas' 10-point loss against the backups didn't bring many positives, but six players finished with double-digit points, including all five starters. Kyrie Irving paced the team with 34 points, while star forward Cooper Flagg had 18 points, 8 rebounds and 6 assists.

Cleveland now gets a much-needed day off and returns to action Monday against the Chicago Bulls. Dallas has its own back-to-back to deal with and will end its three-game road trip on Sunday against the Boston Celtics.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg Passes Kobe Bryant in NBA History With Rare Stat in Mavs' Loss vs. Cavs
articles.summary: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg is officially the second-highest scoring teenager in NBA history.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg is officially the second-highest scoring teenager in NBA history.

Flagg recorded his 1,762nd career point in a Saturday night loss at the Cleveland Cavaliers to pass Kobe Bryant on the NBA's all-time teenage scoring leaderboard.

LeBron James remains the league's most prolific teenager after racking up 2,362 points before the age of 20.

Flagg hit the milestone while posting 18 points on 6-for-19 shooting from the field despite going just 0-for-6 from deep in the 127-117 loss.

The Mavericks shot a combined 32 percent from behind the arc Saturday despite the Cavaliers resting their entire starting lineup due to travel issues .

Flagg still has five weeks and 13 games remaining before he turns 20 on Dec. 21.

He is likely to continue climbing the NBA's teenage scoring leaderboard as he looks to help the Mavericks, which fell to 7-6 with Saturday's loss, avoid slipping further down the standings than 10th in the West.

articles.title: Hezonja muestra su mejor versión el día en que se decide su futuro
articles.standfirst: El alero hace 22 puntos ante los Mavericks coincidiendo con la fecha tope para que los Cavaliers garanticen su contrato
articles.summary: El alero hace 22 puntos ante los Mavericks coincidiendo con la fecha tope para que los Cavaliers garanticen su contrato
articles.body: Por si los Cavaliers aún tenían alguna duda sobre si garantizar el contrato de Mario Hezonja, él intentó aclarárselas con su mejor actuación desde que este verano regresara a la NBA. Aprovechando las muchas ausencias de su equipo, el alero croata fue titular en el triunfo ante los Mavericks por 127-117, jugó 34 minutos, más que nunca, y anotó 22 puntos (9/12 en tiros de campo y dos triples sin fallo), que también son su tope en esta segunda etapa en Estados Unidos. En lo que va de temporada tiene medias de 8,6 puntos, 5,4 rebotes y 1,6 asistencias en 19,3 minutos. Hezonja decidió salir del Real Madrid en junio, justo cuando expiraba el plazo para hacer uso de una cláusula en su contrato que le permitía irse a la NBA, no así a equipos europeos. A última hora, encontró a los Cavaliers, con los que firmó un contrato mínimo de 2,8 millones de dólares que no estaba totalmente garantizado. Hasta el 15 de noviembre podía ser cortado. Su buen papel hasta ahora invitaba a pensar que continuaría. Para reafirmarse, hizo este domingo su mejor partido. Los Cavaliers jugaron sin todos los titulares y también sin su sexto mejor hombre: Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Evan Mobley, Jarrett Allen, Peyton Watson y Sam Merrill. Todos estaban de baja por lesiones, además de haber sufrido los retrasos en los viajes provocados por la paralización de numerosos vuelos este viernes, lo que les obligó a quedarse en Florida tras la derrota ante los Heat. "Hay más conversaciones internas. Ciencia del deporte, entrenamiento atlético, directiva... Se le dedica mucho tiempo y esfuerzo y sé que nuestra prioridad es el bienestar y la salud del jugador, por encima de todo. Así es como abordamos las cosas", argumentó el entrenador Kenny Atkinson sobre las ausencias de sus referentes, aunque los aficionados de su equipo se quejaron por haber pagado por una entrada sin ver a las estrellas. Al menos vieron un triunfo liderado por Hezonja y Tyrese Proctor, que logró su primer triple-doble con 24 puntos, 11 rebotes y 10 asistencias, que igualó o superó sus marcas personales en las tres estadísticas. En los Mavericks destacó Kyrie Irving, antiguo ídolo de Cleveland, que se llevó una ovación al ser presentado y anotó 20 de sus 34 puntos en el tercer cuarto. Cooper Flagg hizo 18 puntos y ocho rebotes. Santi Aldama jugó 16 minutos y metió siete puntos con 2/5 en triples. Fue el único de su equipo con +/- en positivo: con él en pista, Dallas ganó por 16.

articles.title: El Real Madrid repesca a Ndiaye
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot se despidió este sábado de Badalona y se incorpora inmediatamente al conjunto blanco para paliar las bajas de Jantunen y Deck en el puesto de '4'
articles.summary: El ala-pívot se despidió este sábado de Badalona y se incorpora inmediatamente al conjunto blanco para paliar las bajas de Jantunen y Deck en el puesto de '4'
articles.body: Eli John Ndiaye jugó este sábado su último partido con el Asisa Joventut, equipo en el que estaba cedido por el Real Madrid, que ya ha hecho oficial su regreso. En su contrato existía una cláusula por la que el conjunto blanco podía reclamar su vuelta a partir del 15 de noviembre en caso de que necesitara cupos de formación en las competiciones ACB o tuviera muchos lesionados. Ha sucedido lo segundo, especialmente con el puesto de ala-pívot, donde Mikael Jantunen y Gabriel Deck, que puede jugar en esa posición, estarán varios meses de baja. Ndiaye decidió volver a Europa este verano después de una experiencia fallida en la NBA, donde no llegó a debutar con los Hawks en parte debido a las lesiones que sufrió. El Valencia Basket le hizo una oferta, pero el Real Madrid, que en su día le había incluido en el derecho de tanteo, igualó la propuesta taronja y le retuvo. Sin embargo, la acumulación de jugadores capaces de jugar al '4', con los mencionados Jantunen y Deck además de Jaime Pradilla, hizo que se apostara por su cesión para que, a sus 22 años, pudiera tener minutos importantes y seguir desarrollando su juego. El ala-pívot, formado en la cantera madridista, se incorporará inmediatamente al equipo y podría reestrenarse en la Liga Endesa el próximo domingo, casualidades del calendario, enfrentándose a la Penya. Antes hay doble jornada de Euroliga entre semana, con visitas al Besiktas y al Olympiacos. Dado que ya hizo la pretemporada con el Madrid y conoce algunos de los sistemas de Pedro Martínez, podría tener minutos en esas citas si se considera oportuno.

articles.title: Early Report Card Grades for Every NBA Team's Rookie Class
articles.summary: The 2026 rookie class is off to a roaring start, as we could be looking at six (or more) future All-Stars.
articles.body:
The 2026 rookie class is off to a roaring start, as we could be looking at six (or more) future All-Stars.

Sure, we expected top picks like AJ Dybantsa, Cameron Boozer and others to shine, but we've seen some players outside of the top 10 (Yaxel Lendeborg, Meleek Thomas, etc.) get off to hot starts to their careers as well.

It's time to take a spin around the league and hand out grades for every NBA team's rookie class thus far.

Note: The Portland Trail Blazers were the only team not to make a draft selection or play a rookie so far this season.

Kingston Flemings stepping into a starting role after being the No. 8 overall pick wasn't surprising. The fact that the Atlanta Hawks made the move just nine games into the season was, however, especially surprising, since it meant moving veteran CJ McCollum to the bench.

Still, Flemings has played well as a starter, averaging 10.8 points and 3.8 assists in 24.8 minutes while shooting 58.1 percent overall and 50.0 percent from three. The 6'4" point guard has good defensive instincts and could form a good long-term backcourt with Dyson Daniels.

Zuby Ejiofor, the No. 23 overall pick, has recently entered the rotation. He's a skilled big man who can shoot from the outside (44.4 percent) and racked up five assists in just 14 minutes in a No. 6 win over the Washington Wizards, showing off his passing chops.

The Boston Celtics have chosen to go the veteran route in their 9-2 start to the season, with neither Chris Cenac Jr. nor Dillon Mitchell seeing any regular playing time.

Cenac, the No. 27 overall pick, has played just nine total minutes across three games, registering eight points and three rebounds while going 3-for-4 from the field to start his career. The 6'11" big man has a lot of veteran talent in front of him, especially with the addition of Mitchell Robinson.

Mitchell, the 40th overall pick, made his NBA debut in a Nov. 2 loss to the Houston Rockets, going scoreless in his two-and-a-half minutes of play.

Mikel Brown Jr. is already showing why he went No. 6 overall to the Brooklyn Nets, despite the team already having plenty of playmakers.

Even with a small sample size, Brown clearly has the highest upside of anyone on this Nets roster. He's now scored in double figures off the bench in five straight games, mixing in clutch shots with impressive no-look and cross-court passes. Brown's talent pops off the screen, as he'll soon become a full-time starter in Brooklyn.

Joshua Jefferson, the 28th overall pick, has yet to make an impact. He went 0-for-4 in his NBA debut and has logged just three and a half minutes of court time thus far.

Opportunity has been there for Christian Anderson, as the No. 18 overall pick has received a healthy dose of playing time, while the Charlotte Hornets have dealt with injuries at guard.

Averages of just 3.4 points and 1.7 assists in 12.4 minutes while shooting 31.8 percent overall and 19.2 percent from three have been disappointing, especially a 0-of-7 shooting night from deep against the Boston Celtics on Nov. 6. For a guard with size concerns already, Anderson has struggled.

Hannes Steinbach, the 14th overall pick, ranks in the top-10 among rookies in rebounding (4.2) and blocks (0.6) despite playing just 12.6 minutes per game. He's recently played more and grabbed 11 boards while blocking three shots against Boston.

Caleb Wilson is in the running for Rookie of the Year, as he's been one of the few bright spots for a lousy Chicago Bulls team this season.

Among all first-year players, Wilson ranks third in scoring (19.3 points), third in rebounds (6.3), first in steals (1.9) and second in blocks (1.0), while registering a swing rating of plus-15.8 for the Bulls (86th percentile, via Cleaning the Glass ).

The 6'10" forward has been a starter from Day 1 and is a future star in this league.

Dailyn Swain, despite being the 15th overall pick, has made little impact, while Jaylin Sellers is off to a great start in the G League and could switch from a two-way to a standard NBA contract at some point this year.

Meleek Thomas looks like the steal of the draft right now, as the No. 34 overall pick is following up a monster summer league performance with a terrific start to his career.

The 20-year-old guard ranks seventh among all rookies in scoring (13.0 points), second in made threes per game (2.8) and fourth in steals (1.1) and is first in three-point accuracy ( 47.8 percent, min. six attempts ). His mark from the outside is also good for 13th-highest in the NBA .

Thomas plays fearless basketball, as he looks right at home playing alongside future Hall of Famers like Donovan Mitchell and James Harden. Thomas has flat out been better than Harden so far this season, as wild as that is to say about a second-round pick just eight games into his professional career.

There's been a lot of positives from the Dallas Mavericks rookie class, starting with No. 9 overall pick Morez Johnson Jr.

Johnson has all the tools to be an elite defender in the NBA. He doesn't have the imposing size of fellow rookie Aday Mara, although Johnson has shown both rim-protection ability and good hands on defense. The 20-year-old is averaging 7.6 points, 5.1 rebounds, 1.3 assists, shooting 51.8 percent overall in 17.0 minutes off the bench and has picked up a steal in four of his past five games.

Sergio de Larrea has shot the ball surprisingly well so far (50.0 percent overall, 60.0 percent from three) following a poor showing at summer league. We know the passing chops are there, even if the assist numbers don't show it yet (3.9 assists per 36 minutes). No. 48 overall pick, Tobi Lawal, has played sparingly so far.

Trevon Brazile has been one of the most impactful rookies this season, especially on the defensive end. His mobile 6'10" frame helps challenge shooters from all areas of the floor, giving the Denver Nuggets a steal with the 35th overall pick.

Brazile ranks sixth among rookies in rebounding (5.7) and 10th in blocks (0.4) despite being a second-round pick.

Bryce Hopkins, the 49th overall selection, has already started a pair of games for the Nuggets and is shooting an uber-efficient 70.6 percent of his twos and 40.0 percent of his threes through seven games.

At 7-3 overall to begin the year, the Detroit Pistons haven't needed much from rookie point guard Ebuka Okorie just yet. Despite being the No. 17 overall pick, Okorie has yet to crack the rotation, not seeing more than six minutes in any of his first five games.

Still, we've already seen some highlight-level plays from the 19-year-old. Despite his limited 6'2", 185-pound stature, Okorie gets to the basket and can finish in unique and creative ways, given his athleticism.

Totals of 11 points, two rebounds, three assists and a steal in his first 20 minutes of play are encouraging. We just haven't seen enough of Okorie yet to make any real conclusions.

Yaxel Lendeborg could win Rookie of the Year despite being the 11th overall pick. His play as the second-leading scorer on a Golden State Warriors team that has won eight straight games has been a huge surprise this season.

Lendeborg ranks second among rookies in scoring (21.4 points), second in rebounding (7.2), fourth in assists (4.0), tied for fifth in steals (1.0) and fifth in blocks (0.7). He's also shot the ball extremely well, with marks of 52.3 percent overall and 44.3 percent from deep.

Yes, Lendeborg is 24 and far more advanced than the typical rookie, but he's still putting up numbers better than most seasoned veterans while helping the Warriors stay in the playoff race in a tough Western Conference. His play is exactly what the Warriors needed, with Jimmy Butler still recovering from a torn ACL and Draymond Green averaging a career-low 2.8 points per game.

A loaded guard position featuring players like Amen Thompson, Fred VanVleet, Reed Sheppard, Marcus Smart and others has limited the impact rookie Bruce Thornton has made thus far.

The former Ohio State star has logged just 20 total minutes across five games, scoring 12 points on 55.6 percent shooting overall.

A depth piece who should be able to step in and play quality minutes if needed at age 23, Thornton just hasn't been called on much to begin his rookie season.

Tyrese Haliburton's hamstring injury has led to a bigger role for rookie point guard Braden Smith.

The 23-year-old former Purdue star has started each of the last four games for the Indiana Pacers, including a 42-minute performance against the Atlanta Hawks on Nov 2nd, where he put up 19 points, 10 assists, four rebounds, three steals and a block.

Smith's ideal role is a backup point guard in the NBA. His 19 total assists against eight turnovers have been a good start, even as he's struggled with his outside shot (28.6 percent).

The Los Angeles Clippers were blessed with the No. 5 overall pick from the Ivica Zubac trade, which landed them Keaton Wagler.

Wagler, 19, is being used as a sixth man in LA right now as the team has needed his scoring and playmaking while awaiting Brandon Ingram's return from a partially torn Achilles.

Wagler is averaging 12.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 0.8 steals overall while shooting 35.4 percent from three. Unfortunately, he's been one of the NBA's worst finishers from inside the arc, making just 29.7 percent of his twos.

A positive swing rating combined with his 6'6" size is a good foundation to build off of, even if Wagler has struggled with his shot thus far.

Cameron Carr fell into the ideal situation as a three-point shooting wing alongside Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves. Unfortunately for him, the Los Angeles Lakers added a handful of veterans at his position during free agency, keeping Carr mostly glued to the bench for now.

The 21-year-old recently scored his first NBA points on Nov. 9 in a win over the Atlanta Hawks while also grabbing three rebounds in seven minutes of play.

If Reaves, Collin Sexton, Quentin Grimes or another wing misses time, Carr would be in line for more minutes. For now, the 10-2 Los Angeles Lakers haven't needed his services.

Karim López has played limited minutes for the surprisingly good Memphis Grizzlies thus far. Richie Saunders is still recovering from a torn ACL. Cameron Boozer, meanwhile, is playing a major role for a 7-3 Grizzlies team.

Boozer, despite being the youngest player in the NBA, is fifth among all rookies in scoring (16.2 points), first in rebounding (9.7), second in assists (5.5) and seventh in blocks (0.7). The only other player in the league to match or exceed these numbers is three-time MVP Nikola Jokić.

The former Duke star is only being held back by his poor shooting performance. His 42.3 percent shooting from two and 29.0 percent from three are pretty dreadful, although Boozer has provided enough rebounding and playmaking to justify his heavy usage so far.

Ryan Conwell's role has increased as of late, as the 37th overall pick has logged 23.3 minutes over his last three contests.

During this time, the 21-year-old shooting guard is averaging 8.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.3 steals and is shooting 35.3 percent from three.

Having wings who can shoot next to Giannis Antetokounmpo is always important, especially when veterans like Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. are struggling. Conwell is showing signs of being a reliable rotation piece, though we'll need more proof.

Brayden Burries and Nate Ament are big parts of the Milwaukee Bucks' future, as both have shown flashes thus far in their rookie seasons.

Burries was promoted to a starter in his seventh game, demonstrating his all-around game with 21 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and a block against the Toronto Raptors. Overall, he's shooting just 22.5 percent from three this season and 17.4 percent as a starter. Not having a true point guard on the roster hasn't helped.

Ament has shot the ball well (40.0 percent from three), but still looks pretty raw overall. He needs to become more of a ball-mover, as just four total assists in nine games isn't acceptable for anyone.

The Minnesota Timberwolves may be kicking themselves for selecting Isaiah Evans over Meleek Thomas, who went one spot later to the Cleveland Cavaliers. Their two careers have begun very differently.

Evans is out of the Wolves' rotation, even with Anthony Edwards currently sidelined following knee surgery. The 20-year-old shooting guard has appeared in just five games, logging a combined 12 minutes. He's yet to score his first NBA points, going 0-for-3 overall thus far.

Obviously, Minnesota would love to see Evans look NBA-ready now while Edwards recovers. They clearly feel like he's not, despite him being one of the first picks in the second round.

The New Orleans Pelicans didn't own a draft pick until No. 58 overall, when they selected Jaron Pierre Jr. out of SMU.

Currently on a two-way contract, it's unlikely we'll see Pierre play many NBA minutes this season. He's yet to make his debut in the association, although he did score 25 points in his first G League game for the Laketown Squadron.

Expectations should be low for a player who nearly went undrafted, so we won't penalize New Orleans with a bad grade here.

The New York Knicks have leaned heavily on their veterans this season, with rookie Tyler Nickel yet to make his NBA debut.

A sweet-shooting wing who made 41.3 percent of his threes in summer league in Las Vegas, Nickel is currently playing for the Westchester Knicks in the G League.

At age 23, Nickel is one of the older rookies in the league and should be ready to step into a limited role should New York need him.

The Oklahoma City Thunder have been forced to use their rookies more than they likely would have preferred this early in the season, given the vast amount of injuries this team has suffered.

Aday Mara has helped anchor a sixth-ranked defense , as the 7'2" center leads all rookies with 1.8 blocks while ranking fourth in rebounds (6.3). Bennett Stirtz is making 46.2 percent of his three-pointers. Even undrafted rookie Josh Dix has been part of the rotation for stretches.

The Thunder are getting quality minutes from three rookies despite not owning a top-10 pick in the 2026 draft. That's extremely good value, even if all three might be stretched a little thin right now.

Izaiyah Nelson was the 51st overall pick by the Orlando Magic during the 2026 draft. He suffered a fracture in his left ankle during summer league in Las Vegas and has yet to take part in any NBA or G League games to this point.

Currently on a two-way contract, we'll save any grades for Nelson for when he can return to the court.

As gifted a scorer as Labaron Philon Jr. is, shots (and playing time) are going to be hard to come by on this Philadelphia 76ers roster.

Philly is in full championship-or-bust mode this season. The role of "offensive spark off the bench" is already being filled by Anfernee Simons. Philon hasn't shot the ball well (35.3 percent overall, 25.0 percent from three) to begin his career.

Logging a total of 45 minutes across seven games, Philon hasn't shown he belongs in a veteran-heavy rotation just yet.

The final pick of the first round, Koa Peat is still waiting to find a full-time spot in the Phoenix Suns' rotation.

The 19-year-old forward has made the most of his limited minutes, scoring 15 points and grabbing four rebounds in 27 minutes, shooting 60.0 percent overall.

With veterans Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges ahead of him on the depth chart, Peat simply needs to stay productive in his opportunities.

Darius Acuff Jr. should be the leader for Rookie of the Year honors right now, as the 19-year-old point guard already looks like one of the best pure scorers in the league.

His 26.2 points per game not only lead all rookies but also rank 9th overall in the NBA. His 7.3 assists are also No. 1 among all first-year players, placing him at 12th overall in the league.

Acuff plays at his own pace, knowing when to attack an opponent and when to pull back and survey the defense for a better opportunity. His poor early shooting has already improved, as Acuff is up to 41.4 percent from three over his last six games.

The Los Angeles Clippers and Brooklyn Nets should already be questioning their selections at Nos. 5 and 6 overall, as Acuff somehow made it all the way to Sacramento at seven. Emanuel Sharp, the 45th overall pick, is making 40.6 percent of his threes as well.

There's no Victor Wembanyama or Dylan Harper-esque future superstar in this San Antonio Spurs rookie class, as only one of the four draft picks has made much of an impact so far.

No. 20 overall pick Jayden Quaintance is still recovering from a torn ACL and has no timetable for his return. Fellow big man Maliq Brown has played just a single minute this season, while Ja'Kobi Gillespie has logged four.

Tarris Reed Jr., the No. 26 overall pick, is the only Spurs rookie to register any real playing time. The 6'11" center is averaging 2.3 points and 3.1 rebounds in 5.9 minutes over seven games, making seven of his first 11 field goal attempts (63.6 percent).

Now a championship contender, the Spurs don't have much room for rookies in their rotation anymore. At least, none were picked in the late first round or later.

It's been a disappointing start for Allen Graves, the No. 19 overall pick of the 2026. Known partially for his three-point shooting and defense, the 6'9" forward has only connected on 22.2 percent of his outside shots and has a defensive swing rating of plus-3.8 .

The Toronto Raptors will need more from their 20-year-old, especially if Kawhi Leonard continues to miss time.

Jaden Bradley, the 50th overall pick, has played sparingly and isn't a staple in the rotation thus far.

It's been a miserable start to the season for an injury-plagued Utah Jazz team, although the play of No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson has helped ease the pain.

The 6'6" guard ranks sixth among rookies in scoring (15.7 points) and assists (3.8) while his 1.2 steals are second only to Caleb Wilson.

Peterson seems to get more comfortable as the game progresses, with 24.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.3 steals over his last three contests while shooting 45.8 percent from three.

AJ Dybantsa has shown a lot of the flashes that made him the No. 1 overall pick in the draft by the Washington Wizards.

At 6'9", he's a big wing who's a natural scorer at all levels and a strong rebounder. Dybantsa ranks fourth among rookies in scoring (16.7 points), fifth in rebounding (6.1), 10th in assists (2.1) and third in steals (1.1).

He doesn't have the green light as a player like Darius Acuff Jr., playing alongside Anthony Davis and Trae Young, although Dybantsa has a positive swing rating and possesses all the physical tools to be a good defender moving forward.

articles.title: Joel Embiid Injured, Latest Updates on 76ers Star's Status and Timeline for Return
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers are going to be seriously shorthanded at center when they play the Indiana Pacers on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers are going to be seriously shorthanded at center when they play the Indiana Pacers on Sunday.

The team confirmed Joel Embiid will be out with right foot plantar fascia management. Backup bigs Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow will be sidelined as well.

That leaves coach Nick Nurse either starting Tacko Fall at the 5 or utilizing a makeshift center for the majority of the contest.

The new-look Sixers are 10-3 to open the 2026-27 NBA season, an encouraging sign as they try to contend for a championship. Embiid is putting up 17.9 points, 8.8 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 0.7 blocks per game so far this season.

The decorated star is hoping to put together a healthy campaign after struggling to stay on the floor consistently since his MVP campaign in 2022-23. He has yet to play more than 39 games since that season while battling various injuries, mainly a knee ailment.

Embiid still managed to put together a good year when healthy last season, averaging 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game. If he can put up those kind of numbers while staying on the floor consistently, the 76ers will have plenty of success this year.

When Philadelphia added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown this offseason, the only concern fans had was the health of the team's stars. The 76ers will need to continue managing Embiid and his co-stars' playing time so they can ensure a healthy roster going into the postseason.

articles.title: Suns Must Trade for Dejounte Murray for Playoff Push Amid Jalen Green, NBA Rumors
articles.summary: The Phoenix Suns currently sit eleventh in the Western Conference at 5-6 and could be preparing to trade one of their stars.
articles.body:
The Phoenix Suns currently sit eleventh in the Western Conference at 5-6 and could be preparing to trade one of their stars.

Chris Haynes , during an appearance on NBA on Prime, reported that the team has made guard Jalen Green available in trade discussions.

Sam Amick of The Athletic reported, "The outside belief is that they are motivated to swap Green for a proven point guard. The Suns, according to a team source, insist that they'll remain patient with their roster and don't plan to truly engage in trade talks, potentially, until later in the season."

Report: Suns 'Motivated' to Trade Jalen Green 🔄

Regardless of when they talk trades, the team's front office appears ready to part ways with Green if the right deal presents itself.

Enter Dejounte Murray, the star guard for the New Orleans Pelicans, who ESPN's Shams Charania reported has requested a trade from his own team.

Murray is a high-motor playmaker and can create scoring opportunities for his teammates. He is also a pesky defender when necessary. He is currently averaging 31.3 minutes, 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists, 1.6 steals, and 0.6 blocks per game.

The 30-year-old is a more complete player than Green, someone who can be an asset to the Suns on both ends of the floor. While he is older than Phoenix's current star at the position, his defense would help a team that allows 111.7 points per game, according to StatMuse.

Best of all, for the Suns, Murray wants to be there.

The Athletic's NBA Staff reported during a live blog Friday:

"According to a league source with knowledge of Dejounte Murray's situation, the Pelicans' guard has strong interest in joining the Phoenix Suns. His camp has been hopeful that a deal would materialize in which he would be swapped for Suns guard Jalen Green."

They added, "Team sources on both sides recently insisted there had not been any talks between the teams about that deal. But that certainly could change."

Murray's trade value was hurt after he missed all of last season, but he has tools that could help a team in Phoenix with playoff aspirations that does not appear poised to realize them with its current roster.

With the Suns already looking to shop Green, and Murray wanting out of an increasingly frustrating situation in New Orleans, it now feels like the opportune time to make a deal that can right the ship in Phoenix before things get too far out of hand in a loaded Western Conference.

articles.title: 'I don’t know how': Skip Bayless says there's something LeBron James does that's on 'another level'
articles.summary: Skip Bayless’ comments on LeBron James are often negative, but there is something he really admires about the Philadelphia 76ers star. James is one of the gr...
articles.body:
Skip Bayless' comments on LeBron James are often negative, but there is something he really admires about the Philadelphia 76ers star.

James is one of the greatest players to ever play the game. His achievements speak for themselves, and he is often praised by big names in the sport.

Bayless, however, has arguably been the most vocal critic of the 41-year-old, but he has now raved about something James has done over the years.

Skip Bayless says he has no idea how LeBron James has stayed away from surgeries

One of James' biggest strengths is his durability.

The King is in his 24th year in the NBA, and he is still going strong at the age of 41. Nobody has been able to match his longevity at this level in the history of the sport.

The big reason behind that is how he takes care of himself away from the court. That has helped him stay away from any major injuries that required surgery throughout his career.

Bayless has expressed his shock in that regard and admitted that he has no idea how James has been able to avoid a surgery over such a long period.

He said on the Double Coverage Podcast : "Nobody in any sport has been more durable longer than LeBron James.

"I have a close friend who's an orthopaedic surgeon who's worked on a lot of athletes. We were talking the other day: Wait a minute, he's now in year 23 (actually 24), is going on age 42 in December, and he's never had surgery?

"I'm knocking on wood for him, because I don't even want to discuss it. You've never had any knee, no meniscus tear, nothing. And obviously no Achilles. Knock on wood. I don't even want to talk about it. No shoulder issue. Nothing!

"I don't know how he does it. Obviously he takes care of himself. I appreciate that hugely. I relate. But he has it on another level."

James often gets the praise he deserves for his accomplishments on the court, but more people should talk about how well he has looked after himself over the years.

Bayless is right; seeing a player stay away from major injuries for over two decades is almost unheard of in elite sport. It really is incredible.

Hopefully, James can keep that up and continue to make history in the remainder of what has already been a remarkable career in the NBA.
